content.title: About
content.content: Corn pone, baked is a traditional American bread made from cornmeal, milk, eggs, and a small amount of sugar. The batter is baked until a golden crust forms, yielding a dense yet slightly crumbly texture with a distinctive corn aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn pone originated in colonial America as a simple way to use locally grown cornmeal.
It was traditionally cooked in iron skillets or on stone griddles over an open fire.
In some regions it is nicknamed “Indian bread,” although the original recipe differs from Native American dishes.
During the early 20th century it became a staple of Southern home cooking.
Corn pone is often served with honey, butter, or jam.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Cornmeal provides slow‑releasing energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B3 and B5 vitamins aid carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Provides magnesium and iron
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many baked goods, corn pone is low in fat when no additional oil is added.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Cornmeal can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: The traditional recipe is gluten‑free, but adding wheat flour introduces gluten, which is a concern for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn pone can be enjoyed warm, sliced and spread with butter, honey, or jam. It is commonly served alongside soups, stews, or as part of a breakfast plate with eggs and bacon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store baked corn pone in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze, tightly wrapped in plastic.
